article_title: Surveillance and 'constant paranoia': Western diplomats tell BBC of life in war-time Moscow

tasks.prompt: What is the article's central argument about Western diplomacy in Moscow during the war?
options: Western embassies have expanded because contact with Russia is now easier.
Diplomats face surveillance, isolation and practical pressure, yet their limited communication role has become more important.
Diplomats have stopped supporting their own citizens in Russia.
Russian and Western governments now communicate mainly through cultural events.
tasks.correct_answer: Diplomats face surveillance, isolation and practical pressure, yet their limited communication role has become more important.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה מציגה פרדוקס: תנאי העבודה נעשו קשים ומבודדים יותר, אך דווקא בהיעדר ערוצים אחרים חשיבות הדיפלומטים גדלה.

tasks.prompt: What happened to many embassies after diplomats were expelled following the 2022 invasion?
options: They were left short-staffed after reciprocal expulsions.
They replaced all diplomats with local academics.
They received permission to hire unlimited foreign staff.
They stopped being monitored by intelligence services.
tasks.correct_answer: They were left short-staffed after reciprocal expulsions.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: מדינות מערביות גירשו דיפלומטים רוסים, מוסקבה הגיבה בגירושים משלה, ושגרירויות רבות נשארו עם מחסור בכוח אדם.

tasks.prompt: What does “responded in kind” mean when describing Moscow's reaction to expulsions?
options: It offered humanitarian assistance.
It reduced surveillance at Western embassies.
It took a similar retaliatory action by expelling Western diplomats.
It invited the diplomats to return.
tasks.correct_answer: It took a similar retaliatory action by expelling Western diplomats.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: responded in kind פירושו להגיב באותו סוג של צעד; במקרה זה מוסקבה גירשה דיפלומטים מערביים בתגובה לגירוש רוסים.

tasks.prompt: Why did some embassies struggle to pay everyday operating expenses?
options: They had donated their budgets to Ukraine.
Their buildings were closed for repairs.
All embassy staff demanded payment in dollars.
Sanctions cut Russian banks off from Swift and Visa and Mastercard suspended operations.
tasks.correct_answer: Sanctions cut Russian banks off from Swift and Visa and Mastercard suspended operations.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הסנקציות ושיבוש מערכות התשלום הקשו על העברת כסף ועל תשלום הוצאות בסיסיות, עד כדי מחסור במזומן.

tasks.prompt: Why did Pierre Lévy argue against recalling ambassadors after the invasion?
options: He believed worsening relations made a remaining channel of communication more necessary.
He expected trade and joint projects to continue normally.
He wanted embassies to take over Russia's banking system.
He believed surveillance had already ended.
tasks.correct_answer: He believed worsening relations made a remaining channel of communication more necessary.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: לפי Lévy, ככל שהיחסים הידרדרו כך היה חשוב יותר להשאיר נציגים שיכולים להעביר מסרים ולספק תמונה מדויקת.

tasks.prompt: In the article, what does it mean that Russian contacts were “tailed” by FSB agents?
options: They were offered jobs by the embassy.
They were publicly interviewed by journalists.
They were followed and watched as they travelled to the embassy.
They were added to an official guest list.
tasks.correct_answer: They were followed and watched as they travelled to the embassy.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: tailed פירושו שנעקבו פיזית; האורחים הושמו תחת מעקב עד לדלתות השגרירות.

tasks.prompt: Give three examples of surveillance or intimidation described by the diplomats.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להביא שלוש דוגמאות שונות ומדויקות מהכתבה.
expected_points: Diplomats were warned to expect listening devices and cameras throughout their homes.
The FSB tried to recruit two Russian embassy employees to report on the mission.
Russian guests were followed by agents to embassy doors.
Guests at a British ambassador's event were harassed and later questioned by police.
Academics and cultural figures were intimidated into avoiding Western diplomats.

tasks.prompt: Summarise how the war changed both the purpose and the daily operation of Western embassies in Moscow.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לשלב את אובדן שיתוף הפעולה הרגיל, המשימות החדשות, קשיי כוח האדם והכסף, והצורך לשמור על ערוץ תקשורת.
expected_points: Normal work on trade, bilateral relations and joint projects became largely impossible.
Embassies prioritised understanding events inside Russia, communicating official positions and protecting staff.
Expulsions and Russia's ban on hiring foreign nationals caused staffing and maintenance problems.
Financial sanctions created cash and payment difficulties.
With few high-level contacts remaining, diplomats became a rare channel between governments.

tasks.prompt: Why did Lynne Tracy say Moscow was harder than a posting where she had faced direct physical danger?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר את ההבדל בין סכנה מוחשית לבין אי־ודאות מתמשכת וחוסר שליטה, ולתמוך בדוגמאות מהכתבה.
expected_points: In Pakistan she felt that some aspects of the danger remained within her control.
In Moscow, constant counterintelligence pressure created pervasive uncertainty.
Surveillance could extend into private homes and personal contacts.
The resulting constant paranoia could continue even after officials left Russia.

tasks.prompt: Write a balanced paragraph using “persona non grata”, “counterintelligence” and “channel of communication”.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להשתמש בשלושת המונחים במדויק, להציג את המתח בין הסיכון לבין הצורך בדיפלומטיה, ולא לטעון טענות שאינן בכתבה.
expected_points: Explain that reciprocal declarations of persona non grata reduced embassy staffing.
Describe counterintelligence surveillance and recruitment pressure as a source of uncertainty.
Explain why a channel of communication remains valuable when ministerial contacts are rare.
Acknowledge that Russian diplomats also complain of unfair treatment while noting the diplomats' view that Moscow's tactics are broader.
